action: Working session with Rick Tanner to finalize three-location service operational model, contact ASE for EV tech certification pathway, schedule property intelligence conversation with Stephanie Morris, reach out to Mark Thompson with apprenticeship offer
narrative: Patricia Hawkins and Rick Tanner held a two-hour working session that produced an agreed operational framework for the three surviving service lanes — technician transfer targets, throughput capacity estimates, and a shared document both parties are now working from rather than two separate deliverables. Hawkins contacted ASE and learned that group EV certification enrollment for five to eight technicians runs approximately $800 per technician with a six-month timeline, and committed to funding two certifications this quarter while the transfer period keeps those technicians on payroll. She scheduled a market intelligence conversation with Stephanie Morris for next week. She also reached out to Mark Thompson directly with a specific offer: three apprenticeship placements per year across the surviving service locations for graduates of the Millfield Auto Tech Pipeline — a concrete commitment delivered the same week the board voted yes on the program, positioning Regional Auto Group as an early institutional partner rather than a late-arriving opportunist.
